subject: french

rounds.lie: The ending “sportive” describes a sporty man.
rounds.why: “-ive” is the feminine ending, so it describes a woman. A sporty man is “sportif”.
rounds.truth: The ending “sportive” describes a sporty woman.
truths: “Il faut éviter les aliments gras” means “You must avoid fatty foods”.
The ending “gentille” describes a kind woman.
“Je me dispute avec ma sœur” means “I argue with my sister”.

rounds.lie: « un jeu de société » means « a video game ».
rounds.why: Wrong: « un jeu de société » means « a board game ». A video game is « un jeu vidéo ».
rounds.truth: « un jeu de société » means « a board game ».
truths: « je sors avec mes amis » means « I go out with my friends ».

rounds.lie: “Je joue du football” is the correct way to say “I play football”.
rounds.why: Sports take “jouer à”: “je joue au football”. “Jouer de” is only for instruments.
rounds.truth: “Je joue au football” means “I play football”.
truths: “Je joue du piano” means “I play the piano”.
“Faire de la randonnée” means “to go hiking”.

rounds.lie: “Je n'aime pas du tout ça” means “I quite like that”.
rounds.why: “Ne... pas du tout” means “not at all”, so it means “I don't like that at all”.
rounds.truth: “Je n'aime pas du tout ça” means “I don't like that at all”.
truths: “Ça me passionne” means “I'm really keen on it”.
“Il est célèbre pour sa musique” means “He is famous for his music”.

rounds.lie: “Hier je suis allé à un concert” means “Tomorrow I will go to a concert”.
rounds.why: “Je suis allé” is the perfect tense = “I went”. “Tomorrow I will go” is “demain j'irai”.
rounds.truth: “Hier je suis allé à un concert” means “Yesterday I went to a concert”.
truths: “J'ai l'habitude de lire le soir” means “I usually read in the evening”.

rounds.lie: “Assister à un concert” means “to assist (help) at a concert”.
rounds.why: False friend — “assister à” means “to attend”. “To help” is “aider”.
rounds.truth: “Assister à un concert” means “to attend a concert”.
